items.question: Read: 'Maya found a lost puppy in the park. It was cold and hungry. She took it home and gave it food.' Who found the puppy and where?
items.correct_answer: Maya found the puppy in the park
items.passage: Maya found a lost puppy in the park. It was cold and hungry. She took it home and gave it food.

items.question: Read: 'The wizard waved his wand at midnight. Suddenly, the pumpkin turned into a golden coach.' When did the wizard wave his wand?
items.passage: The wizard waved his wand at midnight. Suddenly, the pumpkin turned into a golden coach.

items.question: Read the fable: 'A lion was caught in a net. A tiny mouse chewed the ropes and set him free. The lion learned that even small friends can help.' What is the lesson of this story?
items.correct_answer: Even small friends can be helpful / Don't underestimate others

rubric.full_credit: Identifies moral about small friends helping
rubric.partial_credit: Mentions helping but misses size aspect

items.passage: A lion was caught in a net. A tiny mouse chewed the ropes and set him free. The lion learned that even small friends can help.

items.question: Read the folktale: 'The tortoise challenged the hare to a race. The hare ran fast, then stopped to rest. The slow tortoise kept going and won.' What is the central message?
options: Slow and steady wins the race
items.correct_answer: Slow and steady wins the race
items.passage: The tortoise challenged the hare to a race. The hare ran fast, then stopped to rest. The slow tortoise kept going and won.

items.question: Read: 'Emma's ice cream fell on the ground. She wanted to cry, but instead she took a deep breath and asked for another one.' How did Emma respond to losing her ice cream?
items.correct_answer: She stayed calm and asked for another
items.passage: Emma's ice cream fell on the ground. She wanted to cry, but instead she took a deep breath and asked for another one.

items.question: Read: 'The storm knocked down all the farmer's crops. He felt sad at first, but then he started planting new seeds right away.' What does this show about the farmer?
options: He was too sad to work
items.passage: The storm knocked down all the farmer's crops. He felt sad at first, but then he started planting new seeds right away.

items.question: Read the poem: 'The leaves go swish, swish, swish. The wind goes whoosh!' How do the words 'swish' and 'whoosh' help you hear the sounds?
items.correct_answer: They sound like what they describe
items.passage: The leaves go swish, swish, swish. The wind goes whoosh!

items.question: Read: 'The mouse ran hippity-hop, hippity-hop across the floor.' What does 'hippity-hop' help you understand?
items.passage: The mouse ran hippity-hop, hippity-hop across the floor.

items.question: Read: 'Once upon a time, there was a brave knight. He went on many adventures. In the end, the knight found treasure and lived happily ever after.' How does the beginning introduce the story?
items.passage: Once upon a time, there was a brave knight. He went on many adventures. In the end, the knight found treasure and lived happily ever after.

items.question: A story starts with 'Long ago in a faraway land...' and ends with 'And they never worried again.' What does the ending do?
options: Concludes the action and shows resolution
items.correct_answer: Concludes the action and shows resolution

items.question: The text says: 'The house was very old.' The illustration shows a house with broken windows and peeling paint. What does the illustration add to your understanding?
items.correct_answer: Shows specific details of how old/worn the house is

rubric.full_credit: Explains how illustration adds specific details

items.passage: The house was very old.
items.image_prompt: An old house with broken windows and peeling paint

items.question: The story says 'The children played outside.' The picture shows children building a snowman. What season does the picture show?
items.passage: The children played outside.

items.question: Read two Cinderella stories. In one, a fairy helps Cinderella. In another, fish help her. How are these stories different?

rubric.full_credit: Identifies difference in who helps Cinderella

items.passage: Story 1: A fairy godmother helped Cinderella go to the ball. Story 2: Magical fish granted Cinderella's wish to go to the ball.

items.question: One version of 'The Three Little Pigs' has a wolf who is mean. Another version has a wolf who just has allergies and sneezes. How are these versions different?
Read: 'Elephants are the largest land animals. They use their trunks to drink water and grab food. Baby elephants stay with their mothers for many years.' What do elephants use their trunks for?
items.correct_answer: To drink water and grab food
items.passage: Elephants are the largest land animals. They use their trunks to drink water and grab food. Baby elephants stay with their mothers for many years.

items.question: Read: 'The sun is a star. It gives us heat and light. Earth goes around the sun once every year.' How long does it take Earth to go around the sun?
items.passage: The sun is a star. It gives us heat and light. Earth goes around the sun once every year.

items.question: Read: 'Recycling helps our planet. We can recycle paper, plastic, and glass. When we recycle, we make less trash. Recycling saves trees and keeps water clean.' What is the main topic of this text?
items.passage: Recycling helps our planet. We can recycle paper, plastic, and glass. When we recycle, we make less trash. Recycling saves trees and keeps water clean.

items.question: Paragraph 1: 'Dolphins are mammals that live in the ocean.' Paragraph 2: 'Dolphins breathe air like we do.' What is each paragraph mostly about?
options: Where dolphins live; How dolphins breathe
What dolphins eat; Where dolphins live
items.correct_answer: Where dolphins live; How dolphins breathe
items.passage: Paragraph 1: Dolphins are mammals that live in the ocean. Paragraph 2: Dolphins breathe air like we do.

items.question: Read: 'First, the colonists came to America. Then, they wanted freedom from England. Finally, they fought the Revolutionary War and won.' What happened after the colonists wanted freedom?
items.passage: First, the colonists came to America. Then, they wanted freedom from England. Finally, they fought the Revolutionary War and won.

items.question: Read: 'Water evaporates from oceans. It rises and forms clouds. Then it falls as rain.' What happens after water forms clouds?
items.passage: Water evaporates from oceans. It rises and forms clouds. Then it falls as rain.

items.question: Look at the text with a heading that says 'Types of Birds' in bold. Why is this heading in bold print?
items.correct_answer: To show what the section is about

items.question: A book has a glossary at the back. What would you use a glossary for?
Read the word 'knight'. The letters 'kn' make what sound?
Read the word 'remake'. What does the prefix 're-' mean?
Read this passage aloud with expression: 'Oh no!' said the rabbit. 'My carrot is gone! Who took my carrot?' He looked all around.

rubric.full_credit: Reads with appropriate expression, accuracy, and pace

items.passage: 'Oh no!' said the rabbit. 'My carrot is gone! Who took my carrot?' He looked all around.

items.question: Read this passage smoothly and check for understanding: 'Beavers build dams in rivers. They use sticks and mud. The dams make ponds where beavers live.'

rubric.partial_credit: Accurate but choppy, or fluent but poor comprehension

items.passage: Beavers build dams in rivers. They use sticks and mud. The dams make ponds where beavers live.

items.question: Write your opinion: Is it better to have a pet dog or a pet cat? State your opinion, give at least two reasons, use linking words (because, also, and), and write a conclusion.

rubric.full_credit: Clear opinion, 2+ reasons, linking words, conclusion
rubric.partial_credit: Opinion with 1 reason or missing elements

items.question: Write your opinion about the best season. Tell which season you like best and give reasons why. Use words like 'because' and 'also.' Write a closing sentence.

rubric.full_credit: Names season, gives multiple reasons with linking words, provides closure
rubric.partial_credit: Names season with limited reasons or missing closure

items.question: Write an informative paragraph about an animal you know. Introduce the topic, use at least two facts or definitions, and provide a concluding statement.

rubric.full_credit: Introduces topic, includes 2+ facts, provides conclusion
rubric.partial_credit: Has topic and 1 fact, or missing conclusion

items.question: Write to explain how to make a peanut butter and jelly sandwich. Introduce the topic, explain the steps clearly, and write a closing sentence.

rubric.partial_credit: Steps present but unclear or missing intro/conclusion

items.question: Write a story about a time you tried something new. Include details about your actions, thoughts, and feelings. Use time words like 'first,' 'then,' 'finally.' End with a closing.

rubric.full_credit: Elaborated event, includes actions/thoughts/feelings, temporal words, closure

items.question: Write a narrative about a time you helped someone. Tell what happened in order. Include details about what you did, thought, and felt. Write an ending.

rubric.full_credit: Clear sequence, rich details, includes thoughts/feelings, closure
rubric.partial_credit: Some sequence and details but incomplete

items.question: In your group, discuss what you learned about [topic]. Build on what others say. Ask questions to clarify. Stay on topic.

rubric.full_credit: Builds on others' ideas, asks clarifying questions, stays on topic

items.question: With a partner, discuss your favorite books. Ask your partner questions about their book. Listen carefully and respond to what they say.

rubric.full_credit: Asks questions, listens and responds appropriately, takes turns

items.question: Listen to the text read aloud. Then describe the key ideas in your own words.
After listening to the passage about ocean animals, which is a key detail you heard?
Choose the sentence with the correct past tense verb.
Make this noun plural: 'one box, two ___'
Which sentence uses an apostrophe correctly?
Add commas to this sentence: 'I need apples bananas and oranges.'
items.correct_answer: I need apples, bananas, and oranges.

rubric.full_credit: Correctly places commas in a series
